explain.say: Building a bridge pier in a river is tricky, because pouring concrete and digging foundations need dry ground. A cofferdam is a temporary watertight wall that creates a dry pit in the water.

faq.q: How do you build a bridge pier in a river?
faq.a: Usually by making a dry work area with a cofferdam, or by sinking a caisson. Then the foundations and pier can be built in the dry, or concrete can be placed underwater through a pipe.
A cofferdam is a temporary watertight enclosure, often made of interlocking steel sheet piles, built in water and pumped dry so construction can happen inside.

faq.q: Why doesn't the river crush the cofferdam?
faq.a: Water presses hard on the outside, more so with depth, so the sheets are braced inside with rings of steel beams and struts. Some water still seeps in and is pumped out continuously.

faq.q: What happens to the cofferdam afterwards?
faq.a: Once the pier is above water, the cofferdam is flooded and the sheet piles are pulled out with a crane, ready to be used again on another job.

A caisson is a large box or cylinder sunk to the riverbed that becomes part of the foundation. In pneumatic caissons, compressed air keeps water out of a working chamber at the bottom, as used for the Brooklyn Bridge.
asks: How was the Brooklyn Bridge built?

facts: The Brooklyn Bridge towers stand on pneumatic caissons; many workers suffered decompression sickness, then called caisson disease.
Steel sheet piles interlock along their edges to form a nearly watertight wall.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of a cofferdam?

options.show: Create a dry space to build in water

quiz.why: It keeps the river out so foundations and piers can be built in the dry.

wrong.1: It is temporary and kept empty, not filled with water to store.
wrong.2: It does not generate power; that is a hydroelectric dam.
